title: TwoLeadECG stagewise Q.ANT perturbation decomposition
research_question: On TwoLeadECG disagreement cases, how much of the final reference/Q.ANT logit perturbation originates in the local Fourier/KAN blocks versus the final Q.ANT head and downstream propagation?
hypothesis: Disagreement cases will show substantially larger perturbation already in the concatenated local representation, and propagation of that local perturbation through the reference head will explain more of the end-to-end logit difference than the head's own isolated Q.ANT evaluation error.
scientific_boundary: Diagnostic only. Use the ordinary cross-entropy control from the frozen Exp015/Exp014 architecture and protocol. No architecture, loss, frequency, or TEST-driven tuning.
diagnostics: reference local representation versus Q.ANT local representation
reference head on reference local representation
reference head on Q.ANT local representation
Q.ANT head on Q.ANT local representation
success_criteria: Supported if disagreement cases have higher median local-representation MAE than agreement cases and higher median propagation-only logit perturbation than isolated-head Q.ANT logit perturbation.
promotion_rule: No promotion. The dominant stage determines the next compatibility intervention.
hardware_boundary: Q.ANT CPU/software simulation only; no physical photonic hardware performance claim.
